title: Google adds two TPU systems: one for private data, one for long context
friendlyTitle: Google added two chip systems: one private, one for long jobs
summary: On 9 November Google added TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max, the third and fourth systems in this year's generation. 8tx keeps data and model weights encrypted while they are in use, for regulated inference and private fine-tuning. 8i Max puts two 8i chips on one package, doubling compute, on-chip memory, and memory bandwidth inside the same rack.
friendlySummary: On 9 November Google added two ways to package its latest AI chips. TPU 8tx keeps private data locked while the chip is using it. TPU 8i Max puts two chips in one package so a long document or a large codebase has more memory close by.
whyItMatters: Agents that read a whole codebase, or that handle private records, were running into memory and security limits rather than raw chip speed. These are new system layouts, not a new chip generation. Google also points developers at PyTorch on TPUs, which matters if a team is not already in Google's stack.
friendlyWhyItMatters: A long agent job often stalls on memory, not on raw speed. A regulated job stalls on whether the data is exposed while it is being processed. These systems target those two limits. They are new layouts of this year's chip, not a brand-new chip.
